checks.check: The pipeline crashes, produces invalid outputs, or regressed sharply after integration.
checks.how: Inspect the latest traceback, prediction shapes and ranges, and score history.

checks.check: Recent score movements cannot be attributed confidently to a specific change.
checks.how: Inspect version diffs, repeated-run scores, validation design, and whether a complete baseline exists.

checks.check: Error analysis or ablation history points to missing signal or a mismatch in supplied inputs.
checks.how: Inspect raw samples, input transformations, subgroup errors, and prior feature or data ablations.

checks.check: The current single-model quality has plateaued and alternative compatible predictors exist.
checks.how: Inspect standalone validation results, current architecture, and available trained checkpoints.

checks.check: A trainable model has a measurable optimization or generalization limitation.
checks.how: Read learning curves, objective definitions, fitting configuration, and validation errors.

checks.check: Multiple valid prediction sources exist and their combination may improve held-out errors.
checks.how: Inspect aligned per-model predictions, standalone scores, error correlations, and the active blend.

checks.check: Valid continuous predictions do not match the target scale or required output form.
checks.how: Inspect target values, predicted distributions, subgroup residuals, and the scoring definition.

checks.check: Resource limits or fragile repeated execution block reliable model comparisons.
checks.how: Inspect runtime profiles, memory peaks, failures, and repeated code edits.

checks.check: Sample identifiers or feature columns differ between prediction sources or stages.
checks.how: Compare ordered identifiers, join cardinalities, feature names, and matrix shapes at each handoff.

checks.check: A checkpoint swap introduced missing keys, incompatible dimensions, or tokenizer differences.
checks.how: Compare the checkpoint metadata and saved configuration with the instantiated model, tokenizer vocabulary, and load report.

checks.check: The executed ensemble does not match its configured members or weights.
checks.how: Trace member identifiers and accumulation counts and recompute the blend of a few saved rows by hand.

checks.check: Written predictions have the wrong direction, range, normalization, or source variable.
checks.how: Compare the metric definition and submission schema with raw logits, activated outputs, and the actual saved file.

checks.check: Execution stops at an import, file access, device operation, or library call.
checks.how: Read the first traceback and inspect the relevant installed package, artifact path, argument types, and tensor devices.

checks.check: Substantive changes leave predictions unchanged or a silent fallback bypasses the intended computation.
checks.how: Trace flags and stage outputs on a few identified samples and compare intermediate prediction hashes and provenance.

checks.check: The first failing operation cannot import a module or locate a required file.
checks.how: Read the traceback and compare mounted files, import paths, and installed versions with the configured dependencies.

checks.check: The failing call mixes devices or requests unavailable acceleration.
checks.how: Inspect device attributes, accelerator availability, and the exact error at the failed model call.

checks.check: The failing call uses an unsupported method, argument, or type.
checks.how: Compare the failing call and runtime object types with the locally available function signature and expected return structure.

checks.check: Multiple edits, noisy scores, or a regression obscure the effect of the latest experiment.
checks.how: Review edit history alongside scores and available saved configurations.

checks.check: Local model rankings are unreliable or the split ignores known sampling structure.
checks.how: Inspect fold membership, sample identifiers, target histograms, and train-versus-test population information.

checks.check: Training selects models using a surrogate metric or incorrectly configured callback.
checks.how: Compare callback calculations, prediction shapes, maximize/minimize flags, and monitored datasets against the task metric definition.

checks.check: The raw dataset structure and prediction unit have not been established.
checks.how: Compare the schema, sample rows, identifier counts, and task output requirements with existing exploratory summaries.

checks.check: Several factors changed in the same scored run.
checks.how: Compare the two run configurations and count independently changed settings, features, and members.

checks.check: Observed gains are comparable to prior run-to-run variation or the evaluation set is very small.
checks.how: Read unchanged-run scores, sample counts, seed settings, and artifact timestamps; compare the spread with the claimed gain.

checks.check: A recent change caused a large regression and a verified earlier configuration is recoverable.
checks.how: Compare the regression with historical variation and locate the earlier code, weights, feature list, and preprocessing settings.

checks.check: Repeated nearby settings fail to improve beyond the measured noise level.
checks.how: Inspect the search log for improvement size and direction across successive neighboring trials.

checks.check: No complete and scored end-to-end baseline exists.
checks.how: Check whether one run has produced aligned predictions, the intended metric, and a valid saved submission.

checks.check: One scalar control remains uncertain and earlier trials show a directional response.
checks.how: Inspect the logged parameter values and corresponding validation scores for a bracket around a local optimum.

checks.check: Existing checkpoint results show uncertain agreement between validation and external evaluation.
checks.how: Tabulate paired validation and external scores by checkpoint with preprocessing held fixed and inspect rank agreement.

checks.check: The current baseline is far behind existing evidence and several coupled improvements form a compatible replacement.
checks.how: Compare the current baseline score and design with available trajectory evidence and verify that the replacement components share compatible inputs and outputs.

checks.check: Samples share entities, topics, overlapping windows, or other dependence groups.
checks.how: Count repeated group identifiers and check group overlap between existing training and validation folds.

checks.check: Fold target distributions differ despite otherwise exchangeable sampling units.
checks.how: Compare per-fold label histograms, minority counts, and target quantiles and verify no required grouping is broken.

checks.check: An identifiable training subgroup differs from the expected test population.
checks.how: Compare source or prompt labels and their feature and target distributions with the task description and available test metadata.

checks.check: Current folds leave too little fitting data or unstable validation and out-of-fold coverage.
checks.how: Inspect train and validation counts per fold, coverage of out-of-fold predictions, and fold-score variance.

groups.under: WHAT DOES EXISTING EVIDENCE RULE OUT?

checks.check: Related observations cross current train and validation boundaries.
checks.how: Intersect entity or group identifiers across each split and inspect overlapping source windows.

checks.check: The training examples have imbalance, questionable labels, or incomplete coverage.
checks.how: Inspect class counts, source groups, duplicate identifiers, annotation confidence, and available auxiliary data.

checks.check: The current feature set omits identifiable temporal, semantic, or domain information.
checks.how: Compare raw fields with the feature schema and inspect residual errors by available signal.

checks.check: New features increased dimensionality or earlier ablations suggest some features hurt.
checks.how: Inspect feature counts, importance estimates, cached selection lists, and prior removal results.

checks.check: Current transformations may discard useful information or differ from checkpoint training.
checks.how: Compare raw inputs and inference transformations with the training configuration.

checks.check: Low-confidence labels, duplicates, or a mismatched source subset can be identified.
checks.how: Inspect annotation agreement, duplicate groups, source labels, and errors by quality stratum.

checks.check: Rare classes or relevant subgroups contribute too little to the current objective.
checks.how: Compare sample counts, per-group errors, metric weighting, and current loss weights.

checks.check: The training set is small or imbalanced and plausible label-preserving transformations exist.
checks.how: Inspect class coverage and sample examples under the proposed transform and check the task invariances.

checks.check: Additional labeled data cover relevant cases with compatible targets.
checks.how: Compare source schemas, label definitions, quality indicators, and overlap with existing training samples.

checks.check: Unlabeled in-domain data and a sufficiently reliable teacher are available.
checks.how: Inspect teacher validation accuracy, pseudo-label confidence and coverage, and earlier supervised versus pseudo-labeled results.

groups.under: WHAT DOES EXISTING EVIDENCE RULE OUT?

checks.check: A minority subgroup matches the expected test population and is currently underrepresented.
checks.how: Compare source-group membership, input distributions, and known test metadata.

checks.check: A prior augmentation trial degraded validation without improving minority-group errors.
checks.how: Inspect controlled augmented versus unaugmented validation and per-group residuals.

checks.check: Multiple observations describe each prediction entity but only a narrow summary is used.
checks.how: Inspect records per entity, timestamps, current aggregation functions, and missing-value patterns.

checks.check: Existing aggregates discard ordering or relationships among related fields.
checks.how: Inspect ordered histories, related feature groups, and the current derived-feature list.

checks.check: Text structure or metadata relevant to the target is absent from current representations.
checks.how: Inspect raw documents and metadata alongside existing feature families and errors by length or structure.

checks.check: Sparse text features are noisy, overly narrow, or too high-dimensional for the downstream learner.
checks.how: Inspect vocabulary size, document frequencies, n-gram coverage, and decomposition convergence logs.

checks.check: Available pretrained representations encode information missing from the current tabular features.
checks.how: Inspect available encoder outputs, out-of-fold provenance, feature dimensionality, and prior feature-source ablations.

checks.check: Available signal channels or temporal resolutions are not represented by the current inputs.
checks.how: Inspect channel mappings, signal windows, existing transforms, and trained branch input requirements.

checks.check: Several trained input branches exist and one may add little or harmful information.
checks.how: Inspect existing modality ablations and check that branch toggles have compatible model configurations.

groups.under: WHAT DOES EXISTING EVIDENCE RULE OUT?

checks.check: All model-derived training features were produced by models that saw their own target rows.
checks.how: Match base-model training identifiers against identifiers of each stored prediction row.

checks.check: A ranked feature list exists but its cutoff has not been validated for the current pipeline.
checks.how: Inspect importance stability across folds and previous cutoff-versus-score results.

checks.check: A named feature group is redundant, noisy, or was removed before a regression.
checks.how: Inspect group-level ablation results, missingness, correlations, and the version in which the group changed.

checks.check: A cached selection list predates new features or refers to absent columns.
checks.how: Compare the stored feature-list names and provenance with the current generated schema and fold definitions.

groups.under: WHAT DOES EXISTING EVIDENCE RULE OUT?

checks.check: The only feature importance ranking was computed on data used to evaluate the selected model.
checks.how: Trace fold membership in feature selection and downstream validation.

checks.check: Inference transforms differ from those used to train the loaded checkpoint.
checks.how: Diff saved training and inference transform configurations and compare transformed versions of the same example.

checks.check: Image detail is lost at the current resolution or nearby compatible sizes remain untested.
checks.how: Inspect image and object sizes, trained resolution, prior resolution scores, and memory usage.

checks.check: Current text formatting removes useful content or omits relevant context.
checks.how: Inspect tokenized examples, truncation lengths, whitespace handling, and the formatting used during training.

checks.check: Missing values, unseen categories, or unsuitable numeric scales reach a model that cannot handle them.
checks.how: Inspect dtypes, non-finite counts, category coverage, numeric ranges, and the learner input requirements.

checks.check: Spectrograms lose relevant detail or their dynamic range is dominated by artifacts.
checks.how: Inspect signal spectra and rendered spectrograms, transform parameters, and the trained input representation.

checks.check: The current crop or window excludes potentially relevant neighboring context.
checks.how: Inspect target timestamps, raw window lengths, crop coordinates, and prior center-only versus context results.

checks.check: Known noise frequencies or problematic passbands are present in raw signals.
checks.how: Inspect power spectra, sample rate, filter response, and the filtering configuration used during training.

checks.check: Missing or non-finite values reach a learner with a known missing-value policy.
checks.how: Count missing values by feature and group and inspect native missing-value support and the fitted imputer.

checks.check: Numeric range, resolution, or precision may suppress useful distinctions.
checks.how: Inspect feature ranges, quantization, outliers, and the downstream learner sensitivity to scale.

checks.check: Compatible checkpoints differ in training history or validation quality.
checks.how: Read checkpoint manifests, epoch and stage metrics, and prior standalone comparisons.

checks.check: The current model is underpowered or a different inductive bias is supported by prior errors.
checks.how: Inspect learning curves, standalone model results, available trained configurations, and input modality.

checks.check: Compatible weights pretrained on relevant domain data are available.
checks.how: Inspect checkpoint training provenance and compare domain vocabulary or image characteristics with the target data.

checks.check: A strong backbone uses a limited head or cannot yet combine available branches.
checks.how: Inspect the model forward pass, head dimensions, pooled representations, and current branch outputs.

groups.under: WHAT DOES EXISTING EVIDENCE RULE OUT?

checks.check: The proposed weights were trained with a different input pipeline than the current one.
checks.how: Compare training artifact configuration with the current preprocessing and tokenizer.

checks.check: The current pooling or linear head discards useful spatial, temporal, or hidden-layer information.
checks.how: Inspect the pooling implementation and head capacity and compare existing head-variant results.

checks.check: Extra heads or layers have failed controlled comparisons or overfit.
checks.how: Inspect head ablations and the training-versus-validation gap for the complex variant.

checks.check: Targets are ordered, bounded, or have a useful auxiliary labeling formulation.
checks.how: Inspect target support and correlations and the current output activation and loss.

checks.check: Multiple aligned input branches provide complementary representations.
checks.how: Inspect branch dimensions, modality ablations, and whether current fusion discards branch identity.

checks.check: Tree models show underfitting or overfitting associated with depth or leaf count.
checks.how: Compare training and validation curves and earlier capacity trials on the same feature set.

checks.check: Training fit exceeds validation fit or newly added features increase instability.
checks.how: Inspect the generalization gap, current penalties and sampling rates, and previous regularization trials.

checks.check: Loss curves indicate slow convergence, oscillation, or sensitivity to a changed objective.
checks.how: Inspect per-step losses, gradient scale if logged, current schedule, and stopping time.

checks.check: Training stops before convergence or continues after validation deterioration.
checks.how: Inspect best versus final iteration, patience, maximum budget, and validation trajectories.

checks.check: The current loss does not capture ordinal, ranking, soft-label, or other task-specific errors.
checks.how: Compare the objective with metric penalties and inspect per-target residuals and custom gradient behavior.

checks.check: The raw target encodes censoring, group effects, or offsets poorly represented by the current objective.
checks.how: Inspect target semantics, event and censoring indicators, group distributions, and current transformation code.

checks.check: The current boosting procedure has plateaued or its interface blocks required training controls.
checks.how: Inspect supported early stopping and metric callbacks and results from tuned standard boosting.

checks.check: A component is fitted ad hoc without the fold discipline used by the rest of the ensemble.
checks.how: Inspect that component training code for fold boundaries, validation monitoring, saved models, and out-of-fold coverage.

groups.under: WHAT DOES EXISTING EVIDENCE RULE OUT?

checks.check: A lower learning rate was introduced without increasing the iteration budget.
checks.how: Compare learning rate, maximum rounds, best iteration, and patience before and after the change.

checks.check: Available candidates differ in quality or diversity and the current membership is not settled.
checks.how: Read member manifests and prior standalone and leave-one-out comparisons.

checks.check: A single run or view is unstable and compatible repeated predictions are available.
checks.how: Inspect fold and seed checkpoints, stochastic layers, view invariances, and per-replica scores.

checks.check: Member outputs have different scales or the current combination is not supported by validation.
checks.how: Inspect output distributions, metric invariances, and availability of aligned out-of-fold predictions.

checks.check: A candidate has nonredundant errors and plausible standalone quality.
checks.how: Compare aligned validation residuals and standalone scores with those of current members.

checks.check: One member is consistently weak and a compatible replacement is available.
checks.how: Inspect standalone and marginal scores for the existing member and candidate checkpoints.

checks.check: A member is redundant, harmful in prior blends, or contributes little relative to its inference cost.
checks.how: Inspect error correlations and existing standalone, removal, and full-ensemble scores.

checks.check: A previously better ensemble lost members during a recent change.
checks.how: Compare saved member lists and the corresponding verified ensemble scores.

checks.check: Available fold checkpoints differ in quality or some are currently unused.
checks.how: Check checkpoint existence, split provenance, fold scores, and the current inference fold list.

checks.check: Independent training seeds produce materially different errors.
checks.how: Compare per-seed held-out predictions and scores and confirm checkpoints come from distinct training runs.

checks.check: The task has valid input symmetries or multiple aligned views of the same target.
checks.how: Inspect examples, label invariance, trained augmentations, and earlier view-specific scores.

checks.check: Dropout or other random inference operations are active or being proposed.
checks.how: Inspect evaluation mode and compare repeated forward passes with identical inputs and weights.

groups.under: WHAT DOES EXISTING EVIDENCE RULE OUT?

checks.check: Repeated forward passes with the same weights and inputs are numerically identical.
checks.how: Compare arrays from existing identical-input reruns and inspect evaluation mode.

checks.check: Available fold checkpoints were trained with incompatible feature layouts.
checks.how: Compare saved fold configurations and input schemas.

checks.check: Member quality is similar or previous nonuniform weights fail to beat equal weighting.
checks.how: Compare standalone and blend scores and uncertainty around the claimed weighted gain.

checks.check: Members differ in quality or residual patterns and the current blend has not been retuned after a component change.
checks.how: Inspect aligned saved predictions, standalone and blend results, and the change log; record whether evaluation comes from held-out data or only a small public set.

checks.check: An auxiliary prediction has a stable residual correction that may require subtraction.
checks.how: Inspect residual correlations and prior small positive and negative coefficient probes on held-out data.

checks.check: The metric is ranking-based and member prediction scales or calibrations differ.
checks.how: Read the metric definition and compare member quantiles, rank correlations, and previous rank-versus-raw scores.

checks.check: Models output class distributions and confidence differs across members.
checks.how: Inspect saved logits and probabilities, row sums, and whether the metric penalizes probability calibration.

checks.check: Probability tails or output scale differences dominate an arithmetic blend.
checks.how: Inspect per-member probability histograms and held-out errors in high-confidence and low-confidence regions.

checks.check: Enough aligned out-of-fold examples exist to learn complementary prediction relationships.
checks.how: Verify each training row was excluded from its base-model fit and inspect sample count relative to meta-feature count.

groups.under: WHAT DOES EXISTING EVIDENCE RULE OUT?

checks.check: The only evaluation feedback is a small public subset and many weights have already been tried.
checks.how: Inspect public sample-count information and the number and spread of prior weight-search results.

checks.check: Base predictions contain misaligned rows or inconsistent target direction.
checks.how: Compare identifier order and held-out target correlations for every component.

checks.check: The target is ordinal and the metric depends on discrete label agreement.
checks.how: Inspect unique target levels and metric penalties and compare existing rounding and threshold results.

checks.check: Ordinal label frequencies are approximately known and the metric is sensitive to the marginal prediction distribution.
checks.how: Inspect observed target frequencies, current rounded prediction frequencies, and the metric definition, including penalties for distribution mismatch.

checks.check: Predictions have systematic bias or scale mismatch relevant to the metric or downstream rounding.
checks.how: Inspect calibration plots, held-out residual mean, prediction bounds, and the output activation definition.

checks.check: Observable groups or auxiliary outputs reveal stable group-specific residual bias.
checks.how: Inspect held-out residuals by group and confirm the group or auxiliary signal is available at test time.

checks.check: Previous postprocessing gains vanished after a model change or the transform preserves a metric-invariant ordering.
checks.how: Inspect previous mapping ablations, current prediction distributions, and whether the metric is invariant to the proposed transform.

groups.under: WHAT DOES EXISTING EVIDENCE RULE OUT?

checks.check: Group-specific thresholds were tuned on very few held-out samples.
checks.how: Count validation examples per threshold group and inspect threshold variability across folds.

checks.check: Full runs are slow and new code frequently fails before producing predictions.
checks.how: Inspect stage runtimes and recent failures and identify a small subset that exercises all active stages.

checks.check: Most runtime repeats upstream computation unchanged by the current experiment.
checks.how: Inspect stage timings and compare feature, model, and preprocessing configuration hashes across recent runs.

checks.check: Peak memory grows with full datasets or simultaneously retained models.
checks.how: Read memory logs and inspect tensor and dataframe lifetimes and whether grouping crosses chunk boundaries.

checks.check: Padding, oversized batches, or full precision dominate inference memory or runtime.
checks.how: Inspect length histograms, utilization, out-of-memory traces, batch normalization mode, and numerical sensitivity.

checks.check: Frequent variant edits cause stale paths, mismatched parameters, or accidental component omissions.
checks.how: Inspect duplicated loading logic, configuration diffs, and recurring integration failures.

checks.check: Dead code or intertwined stages obstruct iteration despite a working prediction baseline.
checks.how: Inspect active call paths and duplicated stages and confirm baseline predictions are saved for equivalence checks.

checks.check: Profiling shows repeated metric computation dominates fitting or blend search.
checks.how: Read function-level runtime profiles and compare metric-call time with model and data-processing time.

checks.check: A signal-processing backend fails in the available environment or dominates feature runtime.
checks.how: Inspect backend imports, supported operations, package versions, device availability, and timing of the signal transform.

checks.check: Profiling or loop inspection shows the same conversion or transformation repeats for each group or column.
checks.how: Inspect nested loops and time the repeated host/device conversion or transformation on a representative subset.

checks.check: The dataset or feature matrix is too large even with only one model loaded.
checks.how: Compare peak memory with dataset size and inspect which rows must stay together for entity-level features.

checks.check: Memory accumulates across completed models or feature stages.
checks.how: Inspect live object references and GPU or host memory after each stage; identify objects no later stage uses.
